description: SQL-UDF argument binding follows the DECLARED parameter types, as Snowflake does: a date-flavoured value passed to a TIMESTAMP_NTZ parameter is a TIMESTAMP inside the body, so VARIANT/OBJECT output renders it in full timestamp text ('2026-01-03 00:00:00.000'), never java.time's T-separated form nor date-only text, and DATEADD over it stays in the timestamp domain. Also covers Snowflake's no-underscore TIMESTAMPNTZ cast alias, which appears in real bodies. Converted 1:1 from functions/UdfTemporalParamTest (now retired).

steps.sql:
CREATE FUNCTION wrap_ts(ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ(9)) RETURNS OBJECT LANGUAGE SQL AS
$$ SELECT OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('at', ts) $$

CREATE FUNCTION expiry(ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ(9)) RETURNS OBJECT LANGUAGE SQL AS
$$ SELECT OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('until', DATEADD(DAY, 90, ts)) $$
